messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: Difference between CppAD and TMBad
parts:
A difference between the two frameworks would indicate a bug in TMB, and a bug report would be very much appreciated.
However, it appears from your output that you are comparing a parallel run with a non-parallel run. Therefore, a more likely explanation is that your manual implementation is somehow breaking the rules of parallelization  (using the old PARALLEL_REGION macros?). FWIW automatic parallelization has been available for a while (see TMB help file ?openmp)...

messages.subject: Re: Difference between CppAD and TMBad
parts:
Hi Kasper,

Thank you for your reply. The first run is non-parallel, compiled with "CppAD" (without PARALLEL_REGION in the .cpp):

compile("model.cpp")

dyn.load(dynlib('model'))

The second run is parallel, compiled with "TMBad":

compile(" model.cpp", openmp = TRUE, framework = "TMBad")

dyn.load(dynlib('model'))

ncores = 8

openmp(ncores, autopar = TRUE)

Both use the same model.cpp and the same initial values. I ran them with a subset of the data and obtained the same results. They are now running with the full dataset. Since they are still running, I have not received any bug reports. However, it is weird based on what I have observed so far.

Thanks,

Rujia

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: Difference between CppAD and TMBad
parts:
Looks like you have an overly complex and unstable model. My advice is to start simple, then build up:

- Disable parallelization, use smaller dataset, test with simulated data that the model works, i.e. true parameters are recovered (and positive definite hessian, no NaN sdreport).
- Gradually increase data size, still checking for consistency.
- Finally enable parallelization and check that results are unchanged. Did you get a speedup at all? If not look at other ways to improve speed (BLAS/LAPACK).

If you need more help a minimal reproducible example will be required (ready to run without add-on packages).
